items.title: Cross-Institute Research Mentorship Program registration
items.summary:
Registration is open for the Cross-Institute Research Mentorship Program across University Health Network.
I helped design the program as part of UHN Postdoc Association (UHNPA), working with UHN Office of Research Trainees. It connects trainees with mentors outside their own lab for career advice, support, and connections across UHN.
Program dates: January–May 2027
Time commitment: At least one meeting per month, virtually or in person.
• Mentees: UHN graduate students and postdoctoral researchers. Register as a mentee: https://lnkd.in/gEBigcbu
• Mentors: Experienced UHN postdocs, scientists, scientific associates, PIs, clinician-scientists/investigators, and research staff. Register as a mentor: https://lnkd.in/gpaeZ3-4
If you’d like guidance beyond your own lab or have experience to share, we’d love to have you involved. Certificates are available upon completing the program requirements.
Full program details: https://lnkd.in/gNFSYShJ
Please share with UHN colleagues who may be interested.

items.title: Queen’s Homecoming and alumni mentorship
items.summary:
Celebrating 100 years of Homecoming at Queen's University last weekend was a reminder of the value of staying connected across generations and disciplines.
My PhD years at Queen's School of Computing, within Queen's University Faculty of Arts and Science, shaped my work in AI and my commitment to teaching and mentorship.
For me, alumni connections offer a practical way to contribute: sharing experience, exchanging ideas and helping students navigate their next steps. I’m always glad to connect with students and fellow alumni interested in AI, research or mentorship.
Thank you to the Queen's Alumni team, organizers and volunteers for a memorable weekend.

items.title: Biomedical AI and meaningful evidence
items.summary:
The value of AI in biomedical research depends on how well computational methods address the underlying scientific question.

Attending the 2026 iBEST | Institute for Biomedical Engineering, Science and Technology Symposium, bringing together Toronto Metropolitan University and St. Michael’s Hospital at Unity Health Toronto, was an opportunity to explore research beyond my own area and consider where complementary expertise could lead to collaboration.

As an AI researcher, I’m interested in translating biomedical questions into rigorous computational studies. That involves understanding the limitations of the data, defining the insight we hope to gain and designing validation around the intended application.

Agreeing early on what would constitute meaningful evidence gives a collaboration a clear direction. It guides methodological choices and keeps the work connected to the scientific problem that motivated it.

items.title: Watermarks and fingerprints for content provenance
items.summary: Our new public preprint benchmarks invisible watermarks and content fingerprints as C2PA soft bindings across images, audio and video. The openly licensed benchmark includes reproducible code and recorded results. Preprint; not peer reviewed.

image.alt: Preprint figure comparing watermark and fingerprint success across image, audio and video transformations

items.title: Public manuscript for parameter-efficient SAM adaptation
items.summary: A public manuscript of our SPIE 2026 paper on parameter-efficient fine-tuning of Segment Anything for liver-tumour segmentation is now available on arXiv. It compares LoRA, QLoRA, a convolutional adapter and DiSCo across prompt settings and compute measures. This arXiv manuscript is not a separate peer-reviewed publication.

items.title: Our spectral-adapter research featured by PYCAD
items.summary: PYCAD covered our new DiSECT and SiGA preprint, discussing spectral adaptation of Segment Anything for colorectal liver metastasis segmentation. This is research coverage, not a clinical product announcement.

items.title: Spectral adapters for liver metastasis segmentation
items.summary: Our DiSECT and SiGA adapters adapt Segment Anything for colorectal liver metastasis segmentation. In the 91-case held-out, no-prompt evaluation, SiGA achieved 0.76 Dice on tumour-positive CT slices. Preprint; not peer reviewed.

image.alt: Published diagram showing CT images, SAM encoders, adapters and tumour segmentation masks

items.title: Carotid radiomics study in the September issue
items.summary: Our co-first-author study appears in Ultrasound in Medicine & Biology, volume 52, issue 9, pages 1890–1899. The work combines carotid plaque radiomic features with machine learning for cardiovascular risk prediction.
items.note: September is the journal issue month; the article was first available online on 12 June 2026. No exact September publication day is asserted.

items.title: Multimodal risk prediction in Scientific Reports
items.summary: My co-first-author study combines clinical and CT-derived imaging data for preoperative risk prediction in colorectal liver metastases. Springer Nature published the version of record on 14 October 2026.
